correctness.rationale: PASS. With s=h/2 and R=(I+sL)^(-1), the exact Cayley identity C_h=2R-I reduces all finite connected undirected-graph positivity to R_ii>=1/2. In K_{p,q} the p-part resolvent diagonal is 1/n+(p-1)/[p(1+qs)]+q/[pn(1+ns)]; the q-part diagonal is no smaller for p<=q. Direct rational simplification gives R_ii-1/2=(1+ps-q(n-2)s^2)/[2(1+qs)(1+ns)], yielding h*=[p+sqrt(p²+4q(n-2))]/[q(n-2)] for n>2 and all-h nonnegativity for p=q=1. The p-part first loses positivity beyond the threshold. Independently reconstructed exact rational matrices agree for a biclique grid, including K_{2,3}, h=1, diagonals (-1/35,-1/35,1/7,1/7,1/7). This finite check is not the all-p,q proof.

originality.rationale: FAIL. A published October 4 research result, 'A resolvent-return law for Crank–Nicolson positivity on reversible Markov chains', was identified in a fresh Resultary search and its complete RESULT.md inspected. It proves for arbitrary finite Markov generators exactly C_h>=0 iff every resolvent diagonal is >=1/2, and for every reversible chain the full spectral return-diagonal threshold by eigenprojectors, including a sharp threshold and unconditional-positivity characterization. K_{p,q} with unit edges is one such reversible chain, and its standard four-eigenspace spectrum inserted into that already-published criterion leads to the submitted quadratic and radical by routine simplification. Thus the graph-independent theorem is literally prior, while the named biclique formula is an immediate explicit specialization of stronger prior coverage. Different wording or the novel displayed radical does not avoid implication coverage.
residual_risks: Strong coverage is mathematically explicit; failure does not allege a false formula or invalid finite calculations.
The older reversible theorem gives a general spectral root rather than the biclique radical written verbatim; the equivalence requires standard Kpq spectrum substitution, which is fully established.
